title: Progressive policy-based adoption for Optimize recommendations with human-in-the-loop canaries
creator: Arjun Singh
description:
Problem: Optimize can generate batching and caching config suggestions that materially reduce cost but can regress latency/p99 for some tail workloads. Operators need a low-friction path to accept high-confidence recommendations automatically while retaining safe rollback and an explicit human approval window for higher-risk changes.

Goal: Build a policy-driven progressive adoption framework that: (1) evaluates suggestion risk and assigns a policy tier, (2) executes a staged canary rollout (simulated traffic -> small percent traffic -> ramp), (3) surfaces operator checkpoints (approve/hold/reject) for medium/high risk items, (4) captures rich telemetry during canaries and automates rollback on thresholds, and (5) records audit trails and links to PRs/Playbooks.

Scope: Implement server-side controller + Console UX for: policy assessment, canary orchestration, approval queue, automated validation checks (latency/cost/quality), and deterministic rollback. Work here wires into existing Optimize backend and rollout infra but avoids changing runtime kernel behavior.

Non-goals: Model-training/eval changes, global autoscaling heuristics, or reworking core serving kernel selection. We will not attempt full ML-driven autoapprove in this ticket — instead we expose signals to downstream models later.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recommend pipeline can tag suggestions with policy tier (low/medium/high) via the existing suggestions API.
- Canary controller can execute simulated prefix-replay and a live 5% traffic canary for a single customer and revert automatically on defined SLO breaches.
- Console shows an approval task with one-click Approve/Hold/Reject, plus a link to the telemetry dashboard and diff of config.
- Automated rollback executes within 60s of a rule firing and creates an incident annotation and audit log entry.
- End-to-end test coverage for controller logic and an integration test that runs a simulated canary in CI.
- No regressions in latency for unrelated tenants in smoke tests.
rollout_plan:
1) Backend: Add policy-assessor microservice to tag incoming Optimize suggestions with risk metadata (1 week). 2) Controller: Implement canary orchestration service that supports simulated replay + live percent rollout and rollback rules (2 weeks). 3) Console: Add Approval Queue card, canary status view, and one-click controls with contextual links (1 week). 4) Telemetry: Wire existing per-route dashboards and create a canary dashboard template; add automated alert rules for latency/cost/quality (3 days). 5) Canary beta: limit to internal pilot customers (2 weeks) then expand.

Safeguards: default to manual approval for medium/high risk policies; low-risk rules can be auto-accepted if org opts in. Every automatic change is reversible and recorded.

Escalation: If repeated automatic rollbacks occur for a customer, create a follow-up ticket to pause automated adoption for that org and notify customer success.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for policy-assessor logic and canary controller state machine.
- Integration test in staging: replay recorded requests against canary config and measure token latency distribution.
- Synthetic traffic experiment: create a suite of traffic patterns (short, long context, high-concurrency) and validate rollback triggers.
- Manual QA: Console flows for Approve/Hold/Reject and audit log verification.
- Load test: ensure controller scales to 100 concurrent canaries without added latency to serving layer.
- Post-deploy canary: run internal pilot on two non-production tenants for 7 days and validate metric thresholds.
metrics_and_alerts:
Primary telemetry to capture during canary: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end generation latency, tokens/sec, model throughput, cache hit rate, batch size distribution, per-request cost estimate, error rate (500s/timeout), output quality snapshot (BLEU/ROUGE on deterministic eval prompts).

Automated rollback alert rules (examples):
- p99 latency increase > 25% vs baseline for 10m -> rollback.
- error rate > 1% absolute for 5m -> rollback.
- cache hit rate drop > 15% and cost savings < 5% -> pause.
- quality regression on eval prompts (delta > threshold) -> hold and notify PM.

Alert destinations: Ops Slack channel, Console approval card, and PagerDuty for customer-impacting failures.
comments: 2026-02-26 Arjun S: Drafted ticket after spike with runtime and console teams. Spike showed that simulated-replay catches ~70% of regressions for short-context workloads.

2026-03-01 Maya P: Implemented initial policy-assessor proto. Using a scoring function that weights change-surface (batch size delta), expected cost delta, and historical p99 sensitivity. Posted PR for review: see GH link.

2026-03-04 Lina Z (SRE): Reviewed rollback latency; suggested moving rollback execution to controller sidecar so rollback happens without waiting for orchestration loop. Added note to implementation plan.
2026-03-07 Product review: PM asks that any auto-accept path be opt-in per-org and that we add an audit-visible justification message for each auto-accepted suggestion. Adding to console UX scope.

2026-03-09 QA: Added test vectors for long-context tails; discovered a false-positive rollback in simulated replay for conversation-type prompts — lowered sensitivity for those prompts in policy-assessor and adding additional eval prompts.
2026-03-10 Arjun S: Canary controller core state machine merged to staging. Next: wire approval queue and rollout telemetry, then schedule internal pilot for 2026-03-15.
